section_summary: This section follows U.S. and Far Eastern Commission review of Japan’s draft constitution from July through October 1946. It covers disputes over cabinet membership, suffrage, popular sovereignty, the two houses of the Diet, and the Commission’s authority to review implementing legislation. It ends with a report that both houses passed the amended constitution on October 7.

people.name: Alexander D. Reid

subfiles.title: United States Policy in Regard to the Adoption of a New Japanese Constitution
subfiles.to: United States member of the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Defines U.S. policy on Japanese adoption of a constitution and the Commission’s review authority.
subfiles.summary: The policy says Japan may adopt its constitution through its own procedures if it satisfies surrender terms and Commission policies. The Commission may test the final draft against those requirements but need not formally approve each provision.

subfiles.title: Message Transmitted to SCAP by the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Forwards three copies of a July 15 message concerning press release of constitutional policy.
subfiles.summary: Forwards copies for the Far Eastern Commission and State Department files.

subfiles.title: SWN-4589 Memorandum for Signature
subfiles.about: Routes the SWN-4589 memorandum for signature.
subfiles.summary: Signature routing cover for the preceding memorandum.

subfiles.title: Consultation on Release to Press of Policy Principles
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests an acceptable date for releasing constitutional policy to the press.
subfiles.summary: The Commission accepts delayed release but asks SCAP when publication would be appropriate.

subfiles.title: Filing of July 15 Message
subfiles.about: Transmits the press release consultation message for Commission files.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a copy of the Joint Chiefs’ July 15 message.

subfiles.title: Communication from Far Eastern Commission Chairman
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of the Commission’s constitutional questions to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Asks that the enclosure be sent through the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission Questions on the Draft Constitution
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Seeks SCAP’s views on whether the draft meets Commission policy and the Potsdam Declaration.
subfiles.summary: Raises questions about cabinet selection, suffrage, sovereignty, implementing laws, expulsion of Diet members, and selection of the prime minister.

subfiles.title: Request for Further SCAP Comments
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Asks how SCAP conveyed constitutional policy to Japanese officials.
subfiles.summary: The Department says SCAP’s comments aided the Commission and requests details about suggestions made before final Diet passage.

subfiles.title: Routing Slip
subfiles.about: Routes constitutional correspondence among officials.
subfiles.summary: Lists recipients and routing actions.

subfiles.title: Draft Letter to General Echols
subfiles.about: Requests War Department transmission of a draft message to MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a proposed inquiry about how Commission policy reached Japanese officials.

subfiles.title: Letter to General Echols
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of an inquiry about constitutional policy to MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: Sends the draft message to the War Department for forwarding.

subfiles.title: Enclosed Message on Commission Policy
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Asks what steps conveyed Commission principles to Japanese officials.
subfiles.summary: Requests SCAP’s comments on incorporating necessary changes before Diet passage.

subfiles.title: Further SCAP Comments for the Commission
subfiles.about: Forwards MacArthur’s August 2 response to constitutional questions.
subfiles.summary: Requests circulation of SCAP’s further comments to Commission members.

subfiles.title: Copy of Inquiry on Communication of Commission Policy
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Repeats the inquiry concerning communication of Commission policy.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the request for SCAP’s account of suggestions to Japanese officials.

subfiles.title: SCAP Comments on the Draft Constitution
subfiles.about: Responds to Commission questions about the draft constitution.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur opposes requiring cabinet ministers to sit in the Diet and defends the draft’s treatment of elections and legislative procedure. He expects a clearer statement of popular sovereignty and urges restraint in Allied intervention.

subfiles.title: SCAP Views on the New Constitution
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP’s response for the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Transmits MacArthur’s message at the Joint Chiefs’ request.

subfiles.title: MacArthur’s Reply on the Draft Constitution
subfiles.to: War Department and Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Gives SCAP’s detailed response to Commission constitutional concerns.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur argues that Diet designation of the prime minister and approval of ministers adequately protect democratic government. He addresses suffrage, popular sovereignty, implementing legislation, expulsion, and bicameral procedure. He warns that unnecessary Allied pressure could weaken Japanese acceptance of the constitution.

subfiles.title: July 30 Message Transmitted to SCAP
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of the Commission’s July 30 consultation message.
subfiles.summary: Sends copies for the Commission and State Department files.

subfiles.title: Consultation on the Text of the Constitution
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Transmits the Commission’s questions on the draft constitution.
subfiles.summary: The Commission requests SCAP’s views on cabinet membership, universal suffrage, popular sovereignty, matters reserved for later laws, expulsion of members, and selection of the prime minister.

subfiles.title: Filing of July 30 Consultative Message
subfiles.about: Sends the July 30 consultation message for Commission files.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a certified copy of the message to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Additional SCAP Comments
subfiles.about: Forwards MacArthur’s additional comments on the draft constitution.
subfiles.summary: Requests appropriate action on SCAP’s August 2 message.

subfiles.title: Communication of Commission Policy to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports how SCAP informed Japanese officials of constitutional policy.
subfiles.summary: States that SCAP conveyed relevant principles as suggestions before Diet passage.

subfiles.title: Urgent Request to Consider Cabinet Policy
subfiles.about: Submits an urgent draft paper on cabinet membership.
subfiles.summary: Requests committee consideration of the enclosed policy paper.

subfiles.title: Consultation with SCAP on the Text of the Constitution
subfiles.about: Recommends a U.S. position on the Commission’s cabinet membership rule.
subfiles.summary: Recommends asking the Commission to amend its rule requiring the prime minister and most ministers to belong to the Diet. The appendix recounts MacArthur’s objections and the Commission committee’s defense of the rule as protection against bureaucratic control.

subfiles.title: Revised Request to Consider Cabinet Policy
subfiles.about: Submits another urgent draft paper on cabinet membership.
subfiles.summary: Requests committee consideration of the enclosed paper.

subfiles.title: Revised Consultation Paper on Cabinet Membership
subfiles.about: Restates proposed U.S. handling of the Commission’s cabinet membership requirement.
subfiles.summary: Again proposes seeking amendment of the rule while withholding a veto if the Commission refuses reconsideration. Its appendix reviews MacArthur’s position and the Commission committee’s argument for stronger Diet control of the cabinet.

subfiles.title: London Report on Times Editorial
subfiles.about: Reports a Times editorial on Japan’s constitutional and political developments.
subfiles.summary: The editorial welcomes democratic progress while noting economic inequality and labor concerns. It favors a long-term post-occupation treaty.

subfiles.title: MacArthur on the Final Draft
subfiles.about: Relays MacArthur’s view that the lower-house text can serve as the final draft for review.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur expects little change in principle from the House of Peers.

subfiles.title: Imperial Hereditary Estates Question
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP’s answer about hereditary estates and imperial property.
subfiles.summary: Requests circulation of the September 1 answer to Commission members.

subfiles.title: SCAP Reply on Imperial Property
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Explains the constitutional wording on the Emperor’s property.
subfiles.summary: Says the wording followed Commission policy and imperial property remains taxable.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Draft Reply on Implementing Legislation
subfiles.about: Calls for clarification of Commission review of draft implementing laws.
subfiles.summary: Requests a reply and suggests discussion with Dean Rusk.

subfiles.title: McCoy Letter on Implementing Legislation
subfiles.about: Asks that important implementing bills be filed for Commission review.
subfiles.summary: McCoy says the Commission considers itself competent to review constitutional implementing laws against the Potsdam Declaration and its policies. He proposes filing important drafts when submitted to the Diet and seeking them from SCAP.

subfiles.title: List of Bills on Implementing Legislation
subfiles.about: Lists bills expected to implement the constitution.
subfiles.summary: Names fifteen proposed laws concerning government, courts, finance, elections, and rights.

subfiles.title: Borton Memorandum on Draft Reply
subfiles.about: Submits a draft answer to McCoy’s September 24 letter.
subfiles.summary: Offers the draft as a basis for discussion with Dean Rusk.

subfiles.title: Draft Reply to General McCoy
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Defines a proposed limit on Commission review of implementing legislation.
subfiles.summary: The draft accepts Commission review of enacted implementing laws within its jurisdiction but questions policy decisions on bills before enactment. It suggests a consultative request to SCAP for copies.

subfiles.title: Commission Letter Forwarding Further Constitution Policy
subfiles.about: Forwards the Commission’s September 25 policy decision and minutes.
subfiles.summary: Requests preparation of directives to SCAP under the Commission’s terms of reference.

subfiles.title: Certification of Commission Decision
subfiles.about: Certifies a true copy of the September 25 Commission decision.
subfiles.summary: Certifies the attached decision against the original text.

subfiles.title: Further Policies Relating to a New Japanese Constitution
subfiles.about: Sets further policy on civilian ministers and the two houses of the Diet.
subfiles.summary: Reaffirms civilian ministers and opposes predominance of the House of Councillors.

subfiles.title: Excerpt from Twenty-Eighth Commission Meeting
subfiles.about: Records debate and votes on Soviet constitutional proposals.
subfiles.summary: The Commission unanimously reaffirmed civilian cabinet ministers and opposed upper-house predominance. Other Soviet proposals on sovereignty, ministerial appointments, Supreme Court selection, and regency failed; the Soviet representative then recorded objections to the draft constitution.

subfiles.title: Directive on Further Constitutional Policies
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Transmits the Commission’s September 25 policy for SCAP guidance.
subfiles.summary: Directs attention to civilian ministers, upper-house balance, and implementing laws.

subfiles.title: Supplementary Cable Explaining the Directive
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Explains why the Commission’s policy was transmitted as a directive.
subfiles.summary: Notes that SCAP had already secured the civilian-minister provision. Explains the Commission’s concern about upper-house predominance and says the supplementary cable itself will not be filed with the Commission.

subfiles.title: Request to Send Explanatory Message to SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of an explanation of the constitutional directive.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a message for SCAP’s information.

subfiles.title: Draft Message Explaining Required SCAP Action
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Says the September 25 directive calls for no specific new SCAP action.
subfiles.summary: Explains that SCAP has secured civilian ministers and should supply implementing laws for Commission scrutiny.

subfiles.title: Request to Transmit Draft Directive
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of the Commission’s policy as a directive to MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a draft quoting the September 25 decision.

subfiles.title: Draft Directive on Further Constitutional Policies
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Drafts guidance on civilian ministers and House of Councillors powers.
subfiles.summary: Quotes the Commission’s decision and its intent to scrutinize implementing laws.

subfiles.title: Amendments to New Constitution for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on Diet approval of constitutional amendments.
subfiles.summary: Sends the October 7 CINCAFPAC message for information.

subfiles.title: Diet Passage of the New Constitution
subfiles.to: War Department and Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Reports final Diet passage of the amended constitution.
subfiles.summary: The House of Peers passed amendments on suffrage, lawmaking, and a civilian cabinet; the House of Representatives then approved the amended text. The message says legislative action is complete, with Privy Council action and promulgation still pending.
